$comment: OBS3 — Langfuse score configs for AgentB2C, versioned in git so they're re-creatable on any instance (score configs are project-scoped, no bulk-import API — this file is the source of truth, POST /api/public/score-configs per entry to restore). Mirrors the 16 configs actually created on the project's Langfuse instance on 2026-07-30 (project cms4gd0d20002nz029tuly62e), plus 3 `human_*` configs added 2026-07-31 by OBS7 for judge/human calibration (see observability/langfuse/evaluators.json and evaluation-rules.json), plus `degraded` added 2026-08-24, plus `guard_poi_anchor_coherence` added 2026-08-26 (the 14th guard) — 21 total. Also 2026-08-26: the 3 geo guards' 'not yet wired for emission' note was TRUE and is now stale — the leaf reports them on its A2A DataPart. The 2 date guards remain unwired (still 0.0 on every turn). The contract for the `guard_*` names is GUARD_SCORE_NAMES in libs/b2c_common/b2c_common/scores.py — never rename an entry once it has real data. Exactly ONE name is permanently config-less, and known_gaps explains why it must not be retried.

known_gaps.name: guard_date_hallucinated_year_rolled_forward
known_gaps.reason: PERMANENT — do not retry. 43 chars, and Langfuse hard-caps a score config `name` at 35. Verified 2026-08-24 against the real server (not just inferred from the MCP tool's schema, which was the earlier basis): POST /api/public/score-configs via the langfuse SDK returns 400 {'code':'too_big','maximum':35,'path':['name']}. A config only applies when its name EQUALS the score name, and this score name is frozen by the GUARD_SCORE_NAMES contract (libs/b2c_common/b2c_common/scores.py: 'never rename or remove one') AND now carries real production data (first emitted 2026-08-24T09:50:12Z) — so neither side can be shortened. The score emits fine without a config; config_id only adds UI-side validation. Only a Langfuse-side limit increase would change this.

WIRED 2026-08-26: the leaf reports it on its A2A DataPart (`guards_fired`) and the spine folds it into budget.fired. Before that it emitted 0.0 on every turn.

configs.description: OBS7: human annotator's own hallucination score (0-1, same scale as the 'Hallucination' judge) on an annotation-queue item — for judge/human calibration, not emitted by any code path.

configs.name: human_relevance
configs.description: OBS7: human annotator's own relevance score (0-1, same scale as the 'Relevance' judge) on an annotation-queue item — for judge/human calibration, not emitted by any code path.

configs.name: human_user_distress

configs.name: degraded
configs.description: The one kind of dependency degradation the concierge process can itself observe. Closed set (RGPD: must never become free text) mirrors b2c_common.scores._DEGRADED_REASONS. Created 2026-08-24 via the langfuse SDK: the MCP server's createScoreConfig tool rejects every categoricalCategories payload with a generic 'label value pairs' error, but the SDK accepts that same shape — so that was a tool-side bug, not a payload problem. Use the SDK (or the UI) for CATEGORICAL configs.

configs.name: guard_poi_anchor_coherence
configs.description: Geo guard 14 (AgentB2C-specific, 2026-08-26): a tier-2 Search Box landmark POI thrown away for sitting >100 km from the turn's own anchor (device GPS fix, or the v6 candidate that echoed the city the user named). Closes audit M4 - the echo-back guard validates the NAME, which a homonym passes perfectly (a shop called "Champs Elysees" in Toulon, 830 km from the avenue); this validates the PLACE. hotel_search_agent/geocode_tool.py, wired via the leaf's `guards_fired` DataPart key. No anchor (bare landmark, no city, no GPS) = no-op by design.
